title: hotfix: fix SLO enforcer regional failover ordering that caused cascade load-shedding
author: Priya Raman
ci_status: pass (unit + e2e rerun after flaky integration test)
description: Context: During the incident on 2026-02-18 we observed thrashing between regional failover and SLO enforcement which led to aggressive load-shedding across regions. Root cause: the SLO enforcer applied circuit-breaker state updates asynchronously without a global ordering guarantee; when regional controllers concurrently triggered failover, they raced to mark downstream capacity as 'unavailable' which triggered other regions' enforcers to escalate load-shedding. This PR fixes the ordering and atomicity around SLO enforcer state transitions and tightens backoff/fallthrough logic to avoid cascade failures. Changes: 1) introduce region-scoped compare-and-swap semantics for circuit-breaker state transitions in services/slo-enforcer/state_manager.go to ensure monotonic updates; 2) add a central sequencing token for failover decisions (routing/regional_failover.go) that guarantees idempotent regional failover actions; 3) reduce aggressiveness of instantaneous load-shedding thresholds and add smoothing to SLO violation windowing (configurable via feature flag); 4) add detailed metrics/tags (slo.enforcer.transition_{attempt,success,conflict}) and tracing hooks to make future races easier to debug; 5) add unit tests and an integration test scenario that reproduces the race (tests/slo-enforcer/race_failover_test.go); 6) add a migration to backfill any in-flight state markers in production (tools/migrations/403212_backfill_states.go). Why this approach: making state transitions compare-and-swap prevents conflicting concurrent updates without introducing a global lock; the sequencing token prevents dueling regional failovers while keeping failover decisions local and fast. Rollout plan: feature-gate enabled by default in main for immediate mitigation; monitor slo.enforcer.transition_conflict and slo.enforcer.load_shed_rate during rollout and revert smoothing if we see unintended latency regressions. Checklist: - [x] Reproduced race in integration test - [x] Added unit tests for CAS semantics - [x] Added metrics/traces - [x] Feature-flagged smoothing - [x] Migration script - [x] Reviewed by SRE and runtime teams - [x] CI green after rerun
